introduction: This foundational level introduces the fundamental philosophy of the Specific Relief Act (SRA), 1963. It explains why simply paying 'damages' (money) is not always enough when a contract is broken, and outlines the basic remedies based on the principles of Equity.

core_concepts.title: What is Specific Relief?
core_concepts.description:
While the Indian Contract Act awards 'Damages' (monetary compensation) for a breach of contract, money is not always an adequate remedy. 
- Concept: Specific Relief is a judicial remedy where the court orders the defaulting party to perform the *exact specific act* they promised to perform. 
- Example: If you contract to buy a rare, antique painting and the seller backs out, monetary damages cannot buy you another one. You want *that exact painting*. The SRA allows you to force the seller to hand it over.

core_concepts.title: Civil Rights ONLY (Section 4)
core_concepts.description: A highly tested foundational rule: Specific relief can be granted **ONLY for the purpose of enforcing individual civil rights** and NOT for the mere purpose of enforcing a penal law. You cannot use the SRA to force someone to be punished for a crime.

core_concepts.title: Recovery of Possession of Property (Sections 5 to 8)
core_concepts.description:
The SRA provides quick remedies to recover possession of property if you are unlawfully dispossessed:
- Immovable Property (Land/House - Sec 5 & 6): If a person is dispossessed of their land without due process of law, they can file a suit under Section 6 purely based on 'previous possession' without having to prove absolute 'Title' (ownership), provided they sue within 6 months.
- Movable Property (Goods - Sec 7 & 8): Recovery of specific movable property.

core_concepts.title: The Philosophy of Equity
core_concepts.description: The SRA is rooted in English Equitable principles. Maxims like 'He who comes into equity must come with clean hands' apply here. If the plaintiff themselves acted fraudulently, the court will deny specific relief.

important_entities.name: Section 6 (Recovery of Immovable Property)
important_entities.key_fact: No suit can be filed against the Government under Section 6.
important_entities.significance: If an individual illegally throws you out of your house, you can use Section 6 for quick recovery without proving ownership. However, you CANNOT use this fast-track Section 6 against the Government. Furthermore, no appeal or review lies against an order passed under Section 6.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: If a question asks: 'Can you get specific performance for a contract to buy 100 bags of normal wheat?' The answer is generally NO. Normal wheat is an ordinary commodity. Monetary damages are perfectly adequate because you can just take the money and buy wheat from another seller. Specific performance is reserved for unique items or land where damages are inadequate.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: No Penal, No Govt in Sec 6
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Always remember SRA cannot enforce penal (criminal) laws, and Section 6 summary possession suits cannot be filed against the Government.

exam_strategy_tips: If a Judiciary question asks 'Under which section of the Specific Relief Act can a person dispossessed of immovable property recover it merely on the basis of previous possession?', select **Section 6**.
